channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weak against US Dollar with limited upside – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada ’s (NBC) Stéfane Marion and Kyle Dahms highlight the Japanese Yen (JPY) trading near multi-decade lows around 161 per USD, even as long-end yield differentials move in Japan’s favour.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Bearish bias persists below 0.8600
item.description: EUR/GBP trades with a positive bias on Tuesday as sellers take a breather following the recent selloff that pushed the cross to a more than one-year low. At the time of writing, EUR/GBP is trading around 0.8550 after rebounding from an intraday low of 0.8533, its lowest level since June 2025.

item.title: British Pound: Capped by layered resistance against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the British Pound (GBP) is slightly softer against the US Dollar (USD) after encountering resistance near 1.3400, with limited fresh data and Bank of England (BoE) news.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: “Monetary policy is in a good place”
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of New York President John Williams said on Tuesday that the United States (US) economy continues to show steady, trend-like growth, while the labor market remains stable.

item.title: Aluminium: Short supply supports prices despite Gulf outages – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Barbara Lambrecht says Aluminium’s recent correction has likely run its course, with prices rebounding as Chinese and LME inventories fall sharply and Gulf smelter outages persist.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Japan denies rate-pressure claims as data mixed – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu notes Japan’s Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi rejected reports that the government is trying to push interest rates lower or pressure the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: Gold rebounds modestly despite hawkish Fed rhetoric
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) stages a modest rebound on Tuesday as a subdued US Dollar (USD) lends support, although doubts over the Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate path keep the upside in check

item.title: Oil: Deficits support higher prices – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay argues that Crude Oil is far from oversupplied, with high-frequency global and Chinese balances still pointing to tightness.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Consolidation with stretched USD positioning – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is effectively flat versus the US Dollar (USD) and trading close to their fair value estimate around 1.4158. They expect the recent deterioration in spreads to stabilize, easing downside pressure on the CAD.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy seen on hold through 2026 – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan notes that the Q2 2026 Bank of Canada Business Outlook Survey showed resilient sales and investment expectations despite earlier Oil price shocks.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish NBP tone risks downside – ING
item.description: ING economists Rafal Benecki and Adam Antoniak argue that reduced prospects of further tightening by the European Central Bank (ECB) and Federal Reserve (Fed) should ease external pressure on the Zloty.

item.title: Euro holds steady as traders assess Fed and ECB interest rate paths
item.description: EUR/USD trades in a narrow range on Tuesday as traders await greater clarity on the Federal Reserve's (Fed) and European Central Bank's (ECB) interest rate paths. At the time of writing, EUR/USD is trading around 1.1436, little changed on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Fiscal unease and BoJ path – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the Japanese Yen (JPY) has firmed slightly, pulling USD/JPY back from 162.18 to 161.68, as comments from Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuichi attempt to calm fiscal worries.

item.title: Gold: Price dip seen limited as PBoC buying continues – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes Gold fell to USD 4,120 per ounce after fresh Iranian attacks lifted TTF gas and Oil prices, but Fed rate expectations remain unchanged.

item.title: Euro: ECB support limited by spreads – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada ’s (NBC) Stéfane Marion and Kyle Dahms note the Euro (EUR) fell toward 1.13 in June despite a more hawkish European Central Bank (ECB), underscoring that EUR/USD remains driven by relative rates.

item.title: US ADP Employment Change 4-week average drops to 20K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has further cooled in late June. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 20K jobs per week in the four weeks ending June 20.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ seen starting rate hikes – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) policy decision as the key domestic event, with a first 25 bps hike to 2.50% expected.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Inflation curve debate shapes outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses the Japanese Yen’s (JPY) recent strength and questions whether the Bank of Japan (BoJ) is truly behind the inflation curve.

item.title: Brent: Hormuz security risks support prices – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu reports that a Qatari LNG carrier was struck near the Strait of Hormuz, reviving security concerns and lifting European gas prices and Brent, WTI, Omani and Dubai crude benchmarks.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Dovish inflation path supports more cuts – ING
item.description: Frantisek Taborsky at ING highlights Hungarian inflation falling to 1.7%, below market and National Bank of Hungary (NBH) forecasts, cementing rate cuts in July and August. Markets price around 150bp of easing and a 4.50% terminal rate, with scope for additional cuts.

item.title: Indian Rupee recovers strongly as oil prices remain broadly lower
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) recovers early losses and turns positive against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias held above strong support against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang reports EUR/USD holding near 1.1440 with a firmer underlying tone. The pair is expected to trade slightly higher in a 1.1425–1.1470 range intraday.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Faces pressure near 0.5700 in countdown to RBNZ policy
item.description: The NZD/USD pair is down 0.2% to near 0.5690 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The Kiwi pair faces selling pressure as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) underperforms its peers ahead of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s (RBNZ) monetary policy decision on Wednesday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Trimmed inflation guides rate outlook – Rabobank
item.description: RaboResearch Global Economics & Markets discusses how the Federal Reserve’s new task force on inflation frameworks under Chair Warsh may elevate trimmed inflation in policy decisions.

item.title: European Central Bank: Cautious path to further hike – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas analysts assess recent European Central Bank (ECB) communication from Sintra, highlighting Christine Lagarde’s cautious stance and shift toward “framework guidance” in a volatile environment.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Weakness extends against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that USD/CAD has broken out of a large consolidation and extended gains towards 1.4250, with the upper part of the prior range at 1.4130 now acting as key support.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $60.95 per troy ounce, down 1.79% from the $62.06 it cost on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: High bar for hawkish BoJ repricing – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/JPY is consolidating around 162.00 after touching a 40‑year high near 162.84.

item.title: United States Dollar Index firms as Hormuz tensions boost safe-haven demand
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is holding gains after two successive flat days and trading around 100.90 during the European hours on Tuesday.

item.title: China turns out Gold buyer again
item.description: According to data from the People's Bank of China (PBoC), world’s second-largest economy China increases its Gold reserves again.
